notes.meaning: Jesus saw the growing crowds and walked up the side of a mountain to teach. In Bible times, Jewish teachers sat down to teach, and his disciples gathered around him to listen carefully. He was not running away from the people, but choosing a good place where everyone could hear his message.

Jesus began to speak with earnestness and authority to the crowd. This opening speech begins the famous Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus describes life in God's kingdom. He taught his listeners what kind of character and conduct please God.

To be poor in spirit means knowing that we are spiritually empty and have nothing good of our own to offer God. People who admit their deep spiritual need turn to God like beggars seeking his mercy. God promises that the kingdom of heaven belongs to those who humbly trust him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching often links poverty of spirit to voluntary humility and detachment from worldly wealth, which merit heavenly rewards.

notes.meaning: Those who mourn are people deeply grieved over their own sins and the wickedness around them. This sorrow is not just sadness over life's troubles, but a holy grief that leads people to turn to God. God promises to comfort them with forgiveness and peaceful rest.

Meekness is not being timid or weak, but having gentle strength under God's control. A meek person remains patient when insulted and refuses to take revenge on enemies. Jesus promises that the quiet and humble will one day inherit the earth when God makes all things right.

Hunger and thirst describe an eager, burning desire like that of a person starving for food and water. Believers hunger for true righteousness, which means living right with God and doing his holy will. God promises to completely satisfy this deep spiritual longing.

Merciful people have tender hearts and show real compassion to people who are suffering or in trouble. They readily forgive others because they know how much God has forgiven them. In the final judgment, God will show his rich mercy to those who lived with forgiving hearts.

Being pure in heart means having sincere motives and an inner life cleansed from evil thoughts, greed, and hypocrisy. God desires genuine inner holiness, not merely clean outward religious rituals. Only those whose hearts are cleansed from sin will enjoy the wonder of seeing and knowing God.

Peacemakers do not merely avoid arguments, but actively work to resolve strife and bring people together in love. They follow the example of Jesus by reconciling enemies and promoting God's harmony. Because they show the family likeness of God, they are recognized as his true children.

People who live righteously often face unfair attacks and mistreatment from a world that dislikes God's standards. Living a godly life reproves evil behavior, which can make ungodly people angry. Even so, those who suffer for doing what is right are promised the eternal joy of God's heavenly kingdom.

Jesus warned his disciples that people would insult them, persecute them, and tell vicious lies about them. Believers are blessed only when the evil words spoken against them are completely false and endured for following Jesus. Facing hostility for Christ's sake shows that a believer truly belongs to him.

Jesus tells his followers to celebrate with great joy even when they are mistreated for their faith. God has prepared a wonderful reward in heaven for those who stay faithful under trial. When believers suffer for the truth, they share the exact experience of God's ancient prophets.

Salt keeps food from rotting and adds good flavor, and disciples are called to preserve the world from moral decay. If salt becomes mixed with dirt and loses its taste, it is useless and gets dumped on the street. Followers of Jesus who lose their spiritual distinctiveness fail to help the world around them.

Light makes things visible and removes darkness, and a town built on top of a hill cannot be hidden from view. Disciples reflect Christ's brightness through their holy conduct and the truth they speak. A Christian's faith is meant to be visible to all people.

People do not light a small household lamp only to hide it under a grain bucket. Instead, they put it on a lampstand so its light spreads across the whole room. In the same way, God gives his truth to believers so they will openly help and guide others.

Believers are told to let their good deeds shine openly before the people around them. The goal is never to show off or win personal praise, but to help others see God's goodness. When people see loving and honest actions, they give glory to the Father in heaven.

Jesus did not come to tear down or cancel the Old Testament Scriptures. Instead, he came to fulfill them by keeping the law perfectly, fulfilling its prophecies, and revealing its full meaning. His teaching completes and honors everything God gave through Moses and the prophets.

differ.view: Reformed Christians teach that while Christ fulfilled the ceremonial and civil laws, the moral law remains an ongoing rule of duty for believers.
Lutheran Christians emphasize that Christ fulfilled the entire law for us so that perfect righteousness is given freely through faith.

notes.meaning: Jesus stated that not even the smallest letter or tiny stroke of a pen would vanish from God's law. Everything written in God's word is entirely true and will stand firm until all of God's purposes are accomplished. God's truth is more lasting than the physical heaven and earth.

Anyone who treats God's commands as unimportant and teaches other people to disobey them will be least in the kingdom of heaven. On the other hand, anyone who obeys God's word and faithfully teaches it will receive great honor. God expects his followers to honor every part of his truth in daily life.

The religious leaders of the day focused strictly on external rituals and rules, but their inner hearts were far from God. Jesus warned that no one can enter God's kingdom without a righteousness that goes deeper than outward show. Entrance into God's kingdom requires a true change of heart that produces genuine love for God.

The Jewish teachers recited the commandment against murder and warned people about the local criminal court. However, they limited the commandment to the physical act of killing and ignored the sinful attitudes behind it. Jesus began exposing their shallow teaching to show the deep spiritual meaning of God's law.

Jesus taught that nursing bitter anger and speaking hateful insults make a person guilty before God, just like murder. Calling someone a contemptuous name or treating them with hatred puts a person in danger of eternal judgment. God examines the quiet malice in the heart, not just physical violence.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic expositors interpreted the judgment and the council as referring to temporal penalties in this life, reserving only hell-fire for the punishment of eternity.

notes.meaning: Jesus pictured a worshiper arriving at the temple altar to offer a sacrifice to God. If the worshiper remembers that a brother has a real grievance against him, he must leave his gift behind. Making peace and seeking forgiveness must happen before worship, because God rejects offerings brought with an unforgiving or bitter heart.
